findings.title: Caching allowlist eligibility makes upsampling decisions stale and never invalidated
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist eligibility result in the shared cache for 60s keyed by org + project set. The `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option lookup it is 'optimizing' is already an in-process/option-store cached read, so the added cache buys little while introducing up to 60s of wrong aggregations (count() silently becoming sum(sample_weight) or vice versa) after the allowlist changes. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere, so there is no invalidation path. Recommend dropping the cache layer entirely.

findings.title: Shared cache makes the new endpoint tests order-dependent/flaky
findings.body: Because eligibility is stored in the process-wide cache, the new tests in tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py that patch `options` (allowlisted / partial / empty) can read a value cached by a previously run test for the same org+project key, producing wrong counts and intermittent failures. Tests would need explicit cache clearing, or the cache should be removed.

findings.title: Eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` but passes the enclosing `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard-widget split path the function is deliberately called with `discover` or other split datasets; the decision will therefore be computed for the originally requested dataset, so an errors-only split query can skip upsampling (or a transactions-like split query can wrongly upsample). Pass `scoped_dataset`.

findings.title: Substring match on 'event.type:error' matches negated filters
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does `"event.type:error" in query`, which is also true for `!event.type:error` (exclude errors) and for `event.type:error_something`. A discover query that explicitly excludes errors would then be transformed to sum(sample_weight), returning inflated/incorrect counts for non-error rows. Parse the query or at least require the term not be negated.

findings.title: Error-focus detection ignores the query actually executed
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` reads `request.GET['query']`, but the discover-split code path in organization_events_stats mutates the query (e.g. `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction` / `AND event.type:transaction`). The upsampling decision is therefore made from the original user query and can disagree with the query that is run. The effective query string should be passed into the helper.

findings.title: upsampled_count declares result type 'number' but returns an integer and has no null handling
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64` yet declares `default_result_type="number"`, inconsistent with the sibling count aggregations that use "integer"; clients/meta will report a float type for an integer column. Additionally, events without `sample_weight` (non-upsampled events that may still be in an allowlisted project, or historical data) sum as 0/NULL, silently under-counting; a `sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))`-style fallback would be safer than relying on the schema assumption stated in the comment.

findings.title: Stray git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed
findings.body: The PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d2909 with no corresponding .gitmodules entry. This leaves the repository with a broken/uninitializable submodule and is clearly accidental; it should be removed before merge.

findings.title: Broad silent excepts hide malformed error_sampling context in test factory
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context lookup and the float conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. A test that supplies an invalid `client_sample_rate` will silently produce an event without `sample_rate`, making upsampling tests pass/fail for non-obvious reasons. Validate explicitly (e.g. check types / numeric range) and let unexpected input fail loudly.

findings.title: No test coverage for errors dataset or top-events upsampling paths
findings.body: The new endpoint tests only exercise the default/discover timeseries path. The code adds upsampling transforms in three places (top_events_timeseries, run_timeseries_query/RPC, timeseries_query); none of the top-events or `dataset=errors` paths, nor the dashboard-widget split path, are covered, so regressions in the alias `upsampled_count() as count` handling for top events would go undetected.
